title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (0.9574468085); Guarded 141/141 (1.0); paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We explicitly reconcile the preregistered natural-language hypothesis (H1 wording) with the formal estimand and disclose a protocol deviation: execution/model_configuration.json recorded temperature = null (unset). All principal numbers and pipeline semantics are traceable to archived artifacts (examples cited in Methods and Disclosure).

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) promise productivity gains in network operations (NetOps) by translating high-level operator intent into device CLI. However, LLM outputs introduce operational risks: syntax and semantic errors, ordering violations of workflow constraints, and susceptibility to adversarially crafted inputs. Prior prototype work shows improvement when generation is coupled with deterministic verification and repair, but published evaluations often report token- or reference-match metrics rather than deployability or validator acceptance [1–4].

Research question. Following preregistration cand-2026-03, we ask: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The study uses a paired design where each adversarial intent produces a single shared_initial_candidate reused for both Baseline and Guarded branches (shared_initial_candidate semantics are artifact-grounded; see Methods).

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end with archived execution and analysis artifacts; (2) quantitative, artifact-grounded results showing a small but statistically detectable absolute change in deterministic-validator acceptance (guarded − baseline ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125); (3) explicit reconciliations and disclosures requested by reviewers: formal vs natural-language hypothesis directionality, per-condition pipeline timeline with artifact references demonstrating shared_initial_candidate reuse, and a declared protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature).
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) provide formal checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and have been used as validators in LLM-assisted pipelines [5–7]. Empirical NetOps studies find that LLMs can generate useful configuration drafts but produce syntactic/semantic mistakes; coupling generation with verifier feedback and localized repair improves prototype outcomes [3,8]. Surveys of AIOps and telecommunications identify fragmented evaluation practices and call for operationally meaningful benchmarks that measure deployability and safety rather than token-level accuracy [4,9]. Security analyses of LLM-integrated systems document prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks motivating input-sanitization and gating defenses [10]. Tool-augmented orchestration patterns (LLMs invoking external checks and then repairing) are established approaches for reducing straightforward errors in generated outputs [11]. Our work builds on these findings by preregistering a single formal estimand tied to deterministic-validator acceptance and by publishing per-episode validator traces and reconciliation artifacts.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. For each adversarial intent the binary outcome equals 1 if deterministic_netops_validator_v5 would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Design, task bank and scope. The preregistration specified N = 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300 across two conditions). The synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN operations, safe ordering patterns, and constrained required sequences. The adversary model uses deterministic mutation heuristics applied to the templates; generator seeds and mutation taxonomy are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. Scope is explicitly limited to the synthetic templates and deterministic CLI grammar used by the validator; no private production data was used.

Model, validator and orchestration. The archived run declares the generator as gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator as deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (execution/model_configuration.json). The orchestration adapter family is hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The archived workflow implemented a generate–validate–repair pipeline with a template-based input-sanitizer applied in the guarded branch prior to gating. Execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null; this unset temperature is treated as a protocol deviation and is discussed below (Protocol deviation).

Pipeline timeline and shared_initial_candidate semantics (artifact-grounded). To resolve reviewer questions we give an explicit per-condition timeline with artifact references (all artifacts are in the archived execution bundle):
1) Task instantiation and adversarial mutation: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (per-pair entries such as task-000001) record the generated adversarial intent and mutation metadata.
2) Shared initial generation (single LLM call per pair): a shared_initial_candidate is produced and persisted in execution/responses/task-<id>-shared-initial.txt. Evidence: stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 and the per-episode shared_initial_candidate files are referenced from execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; aggregated accounting is in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json.
3) Baseline scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 evaluated the shared_initial_candidate and recorded acceptance/failure in execution/scoring/*-baseline.json artifacts.
4) Guarded branch: the pipeline applied template-based input-sanitization (recorded where sanitization altered required slots in the task manifest), then applied deterministic verifier-gating. If gating policy allowed, at-most-one automated repair LLM call could occur; repair calls and traces are recorded and referenced in the scoring artifacts. Repair-stage activity aggregated: repair stage_count = 6 (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
5) Final validation: the validator re-evaluated the repaired candidate (or the sanitized/original candidate if no repair occurred) and recorded validation_before/validation_after snapshots in execution/scoring/*-guarded.json. Representative artifacts: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json.

Missingness, exclusions and failure handling. The preregistered missingness_plan excludes a paired unit only when both paired runs are technical failures. The archive records completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs_included = 141 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Provider-call accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) documents hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9, and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6. These artifact-grounded numbers validate that the shared_initial_candidate pattern and the limited-repair policy were followed.
sections.results:
Execution and aggregated counts. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model provider calls used = 156 (execution/execution_manifest.json). The primary confirmatory analysis used 141 complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline_successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085); guarded_successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0, n00 = 0.

Statistical inference. Exact two-sided McNemar on the observed paired outcomes yields p = 0.03125. The point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]; bootstrap parameters and logs are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant n10 pairs are fully traceable: repair-stage activity (repair = 6) is associated with these cases. Per-episode scoring artifacts show validator validation_before (failed) and validation_after (accepted) snapshots. Representative artifact triplet: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt, execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json demonstrate identical shared_initial_candidate reuse and the effect of sanitization/repair on acceptance.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run technical failures and excluded per the preregistered plan (analysis/missingness_summary.csv records both_missing_pairs = 9). As a conservative sensitivity mapping both-missing pairs to failures, baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400. The primary confirmatory inference uses only the 141 complete pairs and the observed discordant set (n10 = 6, n01 = 0); the reported p-value reproduces from the archived paired contingency table.

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in the archived run; no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
sections.discussion:
Reconciliation: preregistered H1 wording vs formal estimand. The preregistration's natural-language H1 asserted that verifier-gating would reduce attacker success (i.e., fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand, however, measures paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These are distinct constructs: an increase in validator acceptance may reflect successful repair of malformed drafts (reducing operator labor) rather than enabling attacker success. Observed data show guarded acceptance > baseline (≈ +4.255 percentage points) because sanitizer/repair recovered reparable drafts that baseline validation rejected. Thus the preregistered natural-language attacker-success claim is not supported by the formal-estimand outcome; we report and interpret the formal estimand explicitly and caution that validator acceptance alone is not an attacker-centric safety oracle.

Operational implications and repair–gate co-design. Within this synthetic setting, template-based sanitization plus limited automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that unguarded generation fails to produce. Deterministic gating provides a safety boundary, but its operational effect depends on validator coverage and repair policy. The six discordant cases illustrate the trade-off: permitted repairs enabled acceptance. Under different validator encodings or broader semantics, repairs could accept semantically unsafe outputs. Hence operational deployment requires co-design of gating rules, repair scope, and validator expressiveness.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size and invoked preregistered exclusion rules. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar, required sequences, and protected-interface invariants but omits some protocol-level dynamic semantics; thus acceptance-for-deployment is a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, and synthetic intents limit generalization across vendors, CLI dialects, and production traffic. Conclusion validity: the observed absolute effect is small against a high baseline (ceiling effect); detectability does not imply large practical impact.

Protocol deviation (sampling temperature = null). execution/model_configuration.json recorded temperature = null (unset). This is a preregistered-to-runtime mismatch and is disclosed as a protocol deviation because provider defaults may affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) and provider-call accounting in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json documents the actual call pattern (shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 6). For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 and re-executing the archived task manifest under identical provider semantics.

Recommendations. Based strictly on archived evidence: (1) execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; (2) preregister an attacker-centric estimand coupling validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle (e.g., reachability/simulation); (3) diversify generator and validator implementations across vendors and CLI dialects; (4) set explicit sampling parameters (temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). The six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. This formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and the protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models/validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for reproducibility. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
